correct: The frozen construction described stages but did not define a measurable sample map.  The replacement fixes the folds, kernels, normalizations, grids, retention threshold, tie rule, localization radius, inversion radius, and fallbacks required by the directive.

The proof uses the newly explicit scan map, the localization lemma, the causal ratio identity, and the displayed model properties directly.  The statement is restricted to the only smoothness face on which the prescribed scan is uniformly centered under the frozen class.

narrow: For \(s>1\), the requested scan is not uniformly centered at \(c_P\)
under the frozen observable-smoothness class.  To see the obstruction,
take \(c_P=1/2\), let the left treatment regression be constant, and let
the right treatment regression have jump \(d_P=\kappa_n\) and a fixed
positive slope \(\gamma\le\min\{M/16,1/8\}\).  These observable
regressions have radius at most \(M\); monotone potential treatment
means can realize them with constant complier probability \(\kappa_n\),
because the unobserved side of each potential-treatment regression is
only required to be continuous.  With common independent fair binary
potential outcomes, the outcome-variance and correlation conditions
also hold.  For \(K_1(u)=4-6u\), direct integration gives, for
\(0\le z\le1\),
\[
 E_P\widehat\Delta_{j,H}^{D}(c_P+zH)
 =\kappa_n(1-4z+3z^2)+\gamma H z(1-z)^2.
\]
At \(z=1/3\) the jump term is zero and the second term is
\(4\gamma H/27\).  Since \(H/\kappa_n\to\infty\) for every
\(s>1\), the population maximizer is separated from \(c_P\) by order
\(H\).  Taking \(n\) large enough makes both empirical scans converge
to that maximizer while \(b=o(H)\).  The fold-four \(K_1\) contrast is
then wholly on the linear right side and converges to zero, so the rule
returns \(\Theta\) with probability tending to one although
\(\rho_n/\kappa_n\to0\).  No strengthening of the sample-size signal
condition removes this deterministic bias.  The proposed restriction
to \(s=1\) is therefore necessary for the prescribed map unless the
model is strengthened by a cross-side derivative restriction, which is
not present and is not proposed here.
